Episode 239. Kelliark and Octavia
Zipfel, Draka.
Kelliark was looking down at his territory, which he had reclaimed after a long time. The garden was all stained with corpses, blood, and flames.
The corpses were all from the Redname Tribe. The magicians trembled as they recalled the authority of Kelliark and Elona, who had burned and killed them all in a single moment.
"To think that we've struggled so much even after securing Elona to deal with these guys... Considering our expectations of him, we can't help but lament, Veradin," Kelliark said in a dry voice.
Octavia, Ronil, and Satrin were standing beside him. Octavia's face still reflected confusion about Kelliark's return, but that was not the case for Satrin and Ronil.
They assisted Kelliark as if he had always ruled Zipfel.
"Ronil."
"Yes, Lord."
"I've read all the records of Veradin's movements that you have kept. There are more than a few disappointing parts."
"It's my fault for not being able to assist properly."
"The role of you and Satrin was not originally that, so it's not a problem. Rather, it's because Veradin didn't use you properly."
Ronil and Satrin.
Kelliark had raised them to be tools entirely dependent on the 'family'. Regardless of who the lord of Zipfel was, Ronil and Satrin always existed as loyal secret weapons.
That's why, now that Kelliark has returned, they were pledging allegiance to Kelliark, who they had once called a rebel, with indifferent faces.
It didn't matter to them who the lord was. Even if an illegitimate child of the Bang family, who was abandoned in an orphanage long ago, became the lord, the two would have behaved the same.
Only Kelliark himself knew that fact. Originally, he intended to take over Veradin's body to live forever, and in the same way, he planned to rule Zipfel forever as its lord, using his descendants.
That's why he needed people like Ronil and Satrin. Monsters who only blindly pledged loyalty to the family and the lord, without thinking.
This was also the reason why the two acted differently from Octavia during the tower's rampage in the past.

At that time, Octavia yelled that they had to save Veradin even if the family suffered a serious blow, while Ronil and Satrin argued that they should give up on Veradin. It was because the lord could be replaced, but the family couldn't.
"By now, Veradin would have passed all the secrets known only to the lord to Runcandel. So, first of all, we need to make the crucial information meaningless."
"What should we do?"
"We'll move the sanctuary. Starting today, the two of you remove all administrators of 2nd grade and below. Also, isolate all administrators of 1st grade and above individually."
"Understood."
"What should we do with the living golems left in the sanctuary now?"
"They're weapons too valuable to destroy. As soon as Elona has some time, she'll manipulate their memories and recycle them, so provide them with enough nutrition to keep them functional until then."
"We will execute your orders."
Octavia could not properly hide her complex feelings that were hard to describe.
It was not easy for her to understand the attitude of Ronil and Satrin, who were familiar with taking orders from Kelliark, and the bold actions of the returned Kelliark.
Therefore, Octavia had been unable to sort out her thoughts for a month already. Kelliark had not given her any special orders yet.
"Octavia."
"Yes."
"It seems you still find it hard to call me the lord. Aren't you glad that I'm back?"
"…That's not it. It's just that I'm confused. Haven't you always looked forward to Veradin, that boy, securing his place as a successor, my lord?"
"That was until he stabbed me in the back."

"Of course, it's true that Veradin betrayed the lord. But that's why it's even harder for me to understand. It seems that Ronil and Satrin have been thoroughly trained by the lord from the start, but isn't it different for me?"
Kelliark gave a gentle smile.
"What are you trying to say?"
"I mean, I don't understand why you're not punishing me. No matter the situation, I have always been loyal to Veradin, who ousted the lord."

"It's a funny thing... In some ways, Veradin was just an experimental subject to you. A valuable experimental subject for all of us. It's like the experimenter swearing loyalty to the experimental subject."
"Please tell me the reason why you're not punishing me. The lord I know would have naturally purged me... or manipulated my mind, like what you've done to Elona and the Marshals now."
"You're overestimating yourself too much, Octavia."
Octavia's eyes widened.

"Since my return, you have never properly welcomed me. Even when some naive and weak individuals who followed Veradin threw their lives at me, you stayed on the sidelines, unable to organize your stance. That's why I spared your life."

"It could mean that you are not worth killing, or that there might be things left for you to dedicate to the family. Or it might also be an acknowledgment of merit. Either way, you've been working with me for a long time for the family."
"I can't understand any better. What exactly do you want me to do?"

"Octavia. Until a few years ago, you were the second-in-command who did not show up externally. The then vice-lord was Andrei, but those who knew thought that the real second-in-command was you. Have you ever thought about why? Why did I have to put Andrei in front and hide you?"
"That's... I thought it was because Andrei was a better card to use and discard than me."
"Exactly. But there's a blind spot. That doesn't mean you were more valuable to me than Andrei. You were the hidden second-in-command because you couldn't do like Andrei."
Kelliark turned around and looked into Octavia's eyes.

"Andrei was crude and not talented. But he was also an excellent co-conspirator. No matter how dirty the tricks I used or the disgusting experiments I continued, I didn't need to explain to Andrei. Because he always understood me."

"And how about you? When we conducted all kinds of experiments, including Sandra and Veradin, you participated in all the atrocities. But you always had an awkward attitude with a face that seemed a bit uncomfortable somewhere. Neither tried to cross the line nor tried not to cross. You just rationalized that everything was for the family and stood in the gray area."
Octavia had no choice but to be shocked.
Kelliark was not wrong.

"What about when Veradin betrayed me? You began to accept the child's name after several attempts to stop Veradin's tyranny. It's the same now that I've come back from hell. You're still standing in the gray area. That's why you couldn't become a vice-lord like Andrei."
Octavia was shivering all over.
She had participated in more experiments and atrocities as the brain of Zipfel than anyone else, but she had never been treated as a strong accomplice by Kelliark.
"Nevertheless, you had magical talent that far exceeded Andrei, and you were always ready to risk your life for Zipfel. In other words, you have excellent power and loyalty, but lack decisiveness."
"So the reason the lord spared me... is because you hope that I will cross the line from now on. Like the lord, like the dead Andrei...."
"Well, you can't inherently become such a person. So don't push yourself. I merely think that it's necessary to have someone like you in our family."
The rising self-loathing brought on nausea. The strong, cold interior she had believed in was roiling like rotten porridge.
As Kelliark said, Octavia had always had an internal negative stance toward the 'experiments.'
She had always covered up those disgusting deeds as being for the benefit of the Zipfel. The ignored truth for a long time, its true face, was choking Octavia.

"So in the future, you just need to continue as you have been, in the grey area. I'll make all the decisions and determinations... as long as you don't betray me like Veradin, you can live as a wraith commander of the Zipfel forever."
Octavia couldn't choose a response.
In the moment she thought perhaps it would be better to die, Kelliark saw right through her.
"Ah, if you're thinking of giving up on life, I won't stop you. Even though the performance is a bit subpar, it would be enough to use you as a bio-golem."
Kelliark approached Octavia and put a hand on her shoulder.

"I wish I didn't have to do such a cruel thing to my sister again. Your mind must be in turmoil, so go back and rest for today. If you wish, you can participate in settling matters with the holy land associates alongside Ronil and Satrin. Or you could assist Elona."
"I retract my statement that I am glad you returned. Facing my true nature, which I didn't realize at this age, isn't easy."
"I didn't expect that I would fall to rock bottom and have to rise up again at this old age, sister. It's a feeling of self-loathing."
"Ronil and Satrin are unlikely to give me any tasks in settling the holy land. Instead, I'll try to calm my mind and support Elona."
"Ah, right. Among the enemy races, there are those who have a score to settle with you. By now, Elona should have almost found their main base, so you can expect good things."
Octavia bowed her head and turned to leave.
When her back disappeared beyond the door, Ragal came to find Kelliark.
"Friend Kelliark, she seems a bit off?"
"Well, she's still family. And Octavia resembles me when I was younger... there was a time when I was like Octavia. In the end, she'll follow me."
"If you say so, but... I'm a bit uneasy. Such kids always cause trouble. I've seen several like that in the Demon Realm. Phaelito was like that too."
"You just focus on injecting poison into Elona. Even if Octavia defies my expectations, controlling that won't be too difficult."
